Definition: prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, μαθέω, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way):--learn, understand.
BiblicalUsage: manthánō is to learn, and it runs through the New Testament as a disciple's word. In Matthew 11:29 Jesus says, learn of me, for I am meek and lowly in heart, and in John 6:45 everyone who has heard and learned of the Father comes to Christ. In Hebrews 5:8 the Son Himself learned obedience by the things He suffered, and in Philippians 4:11 Paul says he has learned to be content in whatever state he is in. Learning here is not information but formation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe manthánō teaches me that discipleship is learning by following, not only by study. I hold that Christ learned obedience through suffering, so I should not expect to learn contentment without cost.
